cards.b: The distance of open water over which the wind has blown. A long fetch produces bigger, more powerful waves.
Low, long wavelength, strong swash and weak backwash. Deposits material and builds up the beach.
High, frequent, strong backwash and weak swash. Erodes material and removes the beach.
Swash: water moving up the beach. Backwash: water draining back down the beach.
Waves force air into cracks in the cliff. The compressed air breaks the rock apart.
Waves hurl sand and pebbles at the cliff, wearing it away like sandpaper.
Water enters cracks, freezes and expands, widening the crack. Repeated cycles break rock off.
Mechanical (freeze-thaw), chemical (rainwater dissolving rock) and biological (roots and burrowing).
Sliding: rock or soil moves along a flat surface. Slumping: saturated soft rock rotates down a curved surface.
Swash carries material up at an angle, backwash returns it straight down. Material zigzags along the coast.
Bands of hard and soft rock lie at right angles to the coast, forming headlands and bays.
Soft rock erodes faster to form bays; hard rock remains as headlands. Beaches form in the sheltered bays.
A flat rock area at the base of a cliff. Left behind when the cliff retreats after undercutting and collapse.
Crack widened to a cave; cave breaks through to an arch; roof collapses leaving a stack; stack erodes to a stump.
A long ridge of sand or shingle joined to land at one end, formed by longshore drift where the coast changes direction.
A ridge of sand or shingle that grows across a bay, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon.

cards.f: Two examples of how people affect coastal landforms
cards.b: Building sea walls and groynes change sediment movement; removing dunes or mangroves reduces natural protection.

gaps.s: Waves with a strong swash and weak backwash are called ___ waves.
Water draining back down a beach is called the ___.
A coastline with bands of rock at right angles to the sea is called a ___ coastline.
A column of rock left standing in the sea after an arch collapses is a ___.
A flat platform of rock at the base of a cliff is a wave-cut ___.
Water freezing in cracks and expanding is called ___ weathering.
Seawater dissolving rocks such as chalk or limestone is called ___.
Longshore drift moves material in a ___ pattern along the beach.

short.q: Describe how a destructive wave differs from a constructive wave.
short.model: A destructive wave is higher and more frequent with a strong backwash, so it erodes the beach. A constructive wave is lower with a strong swash and deposits material.

short.q: Explain how headlands and bays form.
short.model: Bands of hard and soft rock lie at right angles to the coast. The soft rock is eroded faster to form bays, while the harder rock remains as headlands.
points: soft rock erodes faster forming bays; hard rock remains as headlands

short.model: Longshore drift builds a spit across a bay. It grows until it reaches the other side, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon behind it.
points: grows across the bay, trapping a lagoon

short.q: Explain how mass movement affects a cliff made of clay.
short.model: Heavy rain saturates the soft clay, making it heavy and unstable. It slumps down a curved surface, so the cliff retreats quickly.
points: slumps down the cliff, cliff retreats

short.q: Describe the movement of material by longshore drift.
short.model: Waves approach at an angle and swash pushes material up the beach at that angle. Backwash drags it straight down, so material moves along the coast in a zigzag.
points: swash at an angle, backwash at right angles
